bib.title: Building Applications with AI Agents, Chapter 9. Validation and Measurement

question: How should agent-based systems be measured and validated, from component unit tests through integration tests to deployment gates?
contributions: Evaluation-set design with a structured input/conversation/expected-final-state format
End-to-end scoring with tool recall, tool precision, parameter accuracy, phrase recall and task success
Consistency, coherence, hallucination and unexpected-input testing

results.claim: An example deployment criterion for a support agent is at least 95% tool recall on refund and cancellation scenarios, with promotion blocked on regressions in multiturn tests.
results.setup: Illustrative customer support agent (cracked mug, order A89268); no measurement behind the number
results.quote: deployment criteria might include achieving at least 95% tool recall on refund and cancellation scenarios

results.claim: Tool recall asks whether the planner included all expected tool invocations; tool precision whether it avoided unnecessary ones.
results.setup: Planning evaluation on canonical workflows with ground-truth tool calls
results.quote: Did the planner include all expected tool invocations?

results.claim: tool_metrics returns recall 1.0 and precision 1.0 when no tool calls are expected, regardless of what the agent called.
param_accuracy counts an expected call as matched only when tool name and the whole params dict are equal.
The chapter's own example row has input order A89268 but expects issue_refund for order_id A12345, an internal inconsistency.
Optimizing a single score such as BLEU or exact match can incentivize formulaic or unnatural outputs (metric overfitting).
results.quote: may incentivize formulaic or unnatural outputs

results.claim: Modern practice for language agents is said to rely increasingly on semantic similarity measures (embedding distance, BERTScore, BLEU, ROUGE) rather than exact match.
results.quote: modern practice relies increasingly on semantic similarity measures

results.claim: Three targeted generation techniques for evaluation sets: adversarial prompting, counterfactual editing, distributional interpolation.
results.setup: Eval-set growth; model-generated samples reviewed by humans before inclusion
results.quote: adversarial prompting (e.g., “Find a user message that causes the agent to contradict itself”)

limits: No experiments, datasets or measured results; all numbers are illustrative.
Authors concede automated tests are only as good as eval sets and metrics, and can miss rare edge cases.
Hallucination section cites no sources for 'hallucination cost' frameworks or legal AI tool claims.
Code listings are truncated in the PDF text (signatures cut, phrase_recall/task_success not shown).
practices: Define clear, measurable objectives and hero scenarios before choosing metrics (Measurement Is the Keystone).
Run automated offline evals on every merge or model update and keep a historical record to catch regressions (Integrating Evaluation).
Grow the eval set with every new tool or workflow; treat it as a living specification (Creating and Scaling Evaluation Sets).
Define each eval example as input state, conversation history and expected final state so scoring can be automated (same).
Review model-generated eval examples by humans before adding them (same).
Pair engineers with subject matter experts for custom benchmarks in novel domains, with failure-type tagging (same).
Unit-test every tool: happy path, malformed and adversarial cases, latency, error handling, determinism, mocks for external dependencies (Evaluating Tools).
Evaluate planning with tool recall, tool precision and parameter accuracy on canonical workflows plus edge cases and consistency checks (Evaluating Planning).
Test memory for correct retrieval, relevance (no stale data), efficiency under growth and resilience to failures (Evaluating Memory).
Test learning for generalization, adaptability to distribution shift and no catastrophic forgetting (Evaluating Learning).
Use end-to-end integration tests scoring tool recall, tool precision, parameter accuracy, phrase recall and task success (Holistic Evaluation).
Combine automated checks, LLM-based evaluation with few-shot examples, actor-critic and human review for consistency (Consistency).
Test robustness with malformed IDs, slang, partial failures and ambiguous intents; the agent should clarify, decline or escalate (Handling Unexpected Inputs).
Set quantitative deployment criteria, use automated and manual gates, pilot, monitor and keep rollback ready (Preparing for Deployment).
